questions.questionText: WCF stands for:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Windows Communication Foundation.

questions.questionText: WCF is best described as:
options: A unified .NET framework for building service-oriented applications
questions.correctAnswer: A unified .NET framework for building service-oriented applications
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) A unified .NET framework for building service-oriented applications.

questions.questionText: In which .NET Framework version was WCF first introduced?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) 3.0.

questions.questionText: Which protocols are supported by WCF?
options: SOAP with HTTP, TCP/IP, Named pipes
questions.correctAnswer: SOAP with HTTP, TCP/IP, Named pipes
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) SOAP with HTTP, TCP/IP, Named pipes.

questions.questionText: SOAP is:
options: A lightweight protocol used to exchange data over distributed environments
questions.correctAnswer: A lightweight protocol used to exchange data over distributed environments
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) A lightweight protocol used to exchange data over distributed environments.

questions.questionText: SOAP is the underlying layer for:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) ASP.NET Web services (ASMX) and WCF.

questions.questionText: SOAP is maintained by:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) W3C.

questions.questionText: What does ABC of WCF stand for?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Address, Binding, Contract.

questions.questionText: In WCF, the Address specifies:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) Where the service resides (URL).

questions.questionText: In WCF, the Binding specifies:
options: How clients should communicate (encoding, transport, security, sessions)
questions.correctAnswer: How clients should communicate (encoding, transport, security, sessions)
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) How clients should communicate (encoding, transport, security, sessions).

questions.questionText: A service endpoint defines:
options: How the service is exposed to clients
How the database is backed up
questions.correctAnswer: How the service is exposed to clients
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) How the service is exposed to clients.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a feature provided by WCF?
options: Security, performance tuning, and hosting environments
questions.correctAnswer: Security, performance tuning, and hosting environments
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Security, performance tuning, and hosting environments.

questions.questionText: WCF combines benefits of which technologies into a single unified model?
options: Remoting, Web services, Enterprise services, WSE standards, Messaging services
questions.correctAnswer: Remoting, Web services, Enterprise services, WSE standards, Messaging services
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Remoting, Web services, Enterprise services, WSE standards, Messaging services.

questions.questionText: Which are the three main components of a WCF service?
options: Service contracts, host environments, and one or more endpoints
questions.correctAnswer: Service contracts, host environments, and one or more endpoints
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) Service contracts, host environments, and one or more endpoints.

questions.questionText: In the travel analogy, Address corresponds to:
options: The location of the travel agent, station, or airport
questions.correctAnswer: The location of the travel agent, station, or airport
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) The location of the travel agent, station, or airport.

questions.questionText: In the travel analogy, Contract corresponds to:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) The purpose (reaching the destination).

questions.questionText: A service contract consists of:
options: Declarations of methods in an interface
questions.correctAnswer: Declarations of methods in an interface
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Declarations of methods in an interface.

questions.questionText: Message contracts use protocols such as SOAP to:
options: Acquire finer control over the message
questions.correctAnswer: Acquire finer control over the message
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Acquire finer control over the message.

questions.questionText: Policies and bindings in WCF:
options: Apply the conditions required to communicate with a service
questions.correctAnswer: Apply the conditions required to communicate with a service
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Apply the conditions required to communicate with a service.

questions.questionText: Endpoints in WCF are:
options: URIs exposed to the outside world that clients use to connect
questions.correctAnswer: URIs exposed to the outside world that clients use to connect
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) URIs exposed to the outside world that clients use to connect.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a difference between WCF and Web API?
options: WCF supports TCP, HTTP, UDP, and custom transports; Web API supports only HTTP
Web API supports TCP and UDP; WCF supports only HTTP
questions.correctAnswer: WCF supports TCP, HTTP, UDP, and custom transports; Web API supports only HTTP
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) WCF supports TCP, HTTP, UDP, and custom transports; Web API supports only HTTP.

questions.questionText: MTOM stands for:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) Message Transmission Optimization Mechanism.

questions.questionText: Which standards does WCF support for message security, transactions, and reliable messaging?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) WS-* standards.

questions.questionText: WSDL stands for:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Web Services Description Language.

questions.questionText: WSDL is:
options: An XML document that defines the Web service and its contract
questions.correctAnswer: An XML document that defines the Web service and its contract
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) An XML document that defines the Web service and its contract.

questions.questionText: Before creating a service, developers should answer which questions?
options: What functionality, where it is located, and how to send messages
questions.correctAnswer: What functionality, where it is located, and how to send messages
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) What functionality, where it is located, and how to send messages.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the WCF project in the walkthrough?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) StudentWCFServices.

questions.questionText: By default, the WCF project creates which files that are removed in the walkthrough?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Service1.cs and IService1.cs.

questions.questionText: Which attribute marks a model class in WCF?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) [DataContract].

questions.questionText: Which attribute marks each property in a data contract?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) [DataMember].

questions.questionText: Which attribute is applied to methods in a WCF service interface?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) [OperationContract].

questions.questionText: Which namespace contains ServiceContract and OperationContract?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) System.ServiceModel.

questions.questionText: In the walkthrough, which binding is used for the main service endpoint?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) basicHttpBinding.

questions.questionText: The Metadata Exchange endpoint is used by the service to:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Describe itself to clients.

questions.questionText: Which tool is embedded in Visual Studio for testing WCF services?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) WCF Test Client.

questions.questionText: Each endpoint in WCF configuration consists of how many properties?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) Four (Address, Binding, Contract, Behaviors).

questions.questionText: Which attribute in the endpoint specifies the binding policy such as wsHttpBinding?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) binding.

questions.questionText: Which categories of information are enclosed in a binding?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Protocols, encoding, and transport.

questions.questionText: Which binding suits connecting to services that adapt to WS-I Basic Profile (e.g., ASP.NET Web services)?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) BasicHttpBinding.

questions.questionText: Which binding is suited for a local network with higher performance than HTTP bindings?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) NetTcpBinding.

questions.questionText: Which binding connects to other WCF endpoints on the same machine?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) NetNamedPipeBinding.

questions.questionText: Which binding uses queued messages with other WCF endpoints?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) NetMsmqBinding.

questions.questionText: A Service Bus works on which concept?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Multi-tenant.

questions.questionText: Hybrid applications are:
options: Enterprise applications based on Azure that may use local components difficult to migrate to the cloud
questions.correctAnswer: Enterprise applications based on Azure that may use local components difficult to migrate to the cloud
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) Enterprise applications based on Azure that may use local components difficult to migrate to the cloud.

questions.questionText: Relayed messaging offers:
options: Request/response, one-way, peer-to-peer, and direct TCP messaging
questions.correctAnswer: Request/response, one-way, peer-to-peer, and direct TCP messaging
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Request/response, one-way, peer-to-peer, and direct TCP messaging.

questions.questionText: Brokered messaging offers:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Subscriptions, topics, and queues (asynchronous messaging).

questions.questionText: Which section in the namespace page is used to get keys and connection strings?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) Shared access policies.

questions.questionText: Which NuGet package is installed for Service Bus integration in the WCF app?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) Microsoft Azure Service Bus.

questions.questionText: Which binding is used for the Service Bus relay endpoint in the sample?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) netTcpRelayBinding.

questions.questionText: Which tool downloads metadata from running services and saves it locally?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is B) Svcutil.exe.

questions.questionText: Svcutil.exe retrieves metadata using:
options: WS-MetadataExchange (and XML Web Service Directory for HTTP/HTTPS)
questions.correctAnswer: WS-MetadataExchange (and XML Web Service Directory for HTTP/HTTPS)
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) WS-MetadataExchange (and XML Web Service Directory for HTTP/HTTPS).

questions.questionText: Svcutil.exe generates which binding for a service with a BasicHttpContextBinding endpoint?
options: BasicHttpBinding with allowCookies set to true
questions.correctAnswer: BasicHttpBinding with allowCookies set to true
questions.explanation: Correct answer is D) BasicHttpBinding with allowCookies set to true.

questions.questionText: Which Svcutil.exe option is used in the sample command to specify the metadata output directory?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is A) /d:.

questions.questionText: A proxy class:
options: Maps parameters to XML elements so clients need not communicate at the SOAP level
questions.correctAnswer: Maps parameters to XML elements so clients need not communicate at the SOAP level
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Maps parameters to XML elements so clients need not communicate at the SOAP level.

questions.questionText: Which Visual Studio feature generates a WCF client proxy?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is C) Add Service Reference.
